# EventKind

**PPL language/runtime 4.00 - enum.**

[Object model and calling conventions](../objects.md) | [API index](index.md)

Use qualified values rather than raw integers. These are open nominal enums: each enum has its own type, and its known values are listed below. Host operations may reject unknown or unsupported values even though the enum can store them. See [enum rules and bit operations](../../../new_ppl.md#enum--endenum-declaration-350).

The default value is `EventKind.None` (the first declared member).

## Values

| Name | Integer value | Meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `EventKind.None` | `0` | No event was available, for example after a non-blocking `Poll` or a timed-out `Wait`. |
| `EventKind.Key` | `1` | Selects which `EVENT` property group is meaningful: translated key, physical key edge, mouse, queue overflow, or audio completion. |
| `EventKind.KeyEdge` | `2` | Selects which `EVENT` property group is meaningful: translated key, physical key edge, mouse, queue overflow, or audio completion. |
| `EventKind.Mouse` | `3` | Selects which `EVENT` property group is meaningful: translated key, physical key edge, mouse, queue overflow, or audio completion. |
| `EventKind.Overflow` | `4` | Selects which `EVENT` property group is meaningful: translated key, physical key edge, mouse, queue overflow, or audio completion. |
| `EventKind.Audio` | `5` | Selects which `EVENT` property group is meaningful: translated key, physical key edge, mouse, queue overflow, or audio completion. |
| `EventKind.Resize` | `6` | The logical text size changed. Read a fresh `Terminal.Info` for `Columns`/`Rows`; stored snapshots remain unchanged. Only `Kind` and `Time` are meaningful. Rapid changes may coalesce into the latest size; identical sizes do not notify. No input mode or keypress is needed, and resize does not reset idle time. Sources: Telnet NAWS and logical ANSI/board resizing; NAWS is limited to 132 columns and 60 rows. |

## Has

```PPL
EventKind.Has(EventKind mask) BOOLEAN
```

Instance function.

Returns BOOLEAN: true if all bits in the mask are set. Receiver and mask must have the same enum type and are evaluated once, receiver first. No intermediate enum value is constructed. A zero mask always returns true; use equality with the zero member to test that no bits are set. Available from language 350; requires runtime 400.
